blocks.x: Cloud, Edge & Platform applied to Advertising & MarTech. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Ad and martech businesses trade on identity, measurement and trust: signal loss (cookie deprecation, ATT), clean-room measurement and consent architecture decide whether targeting survives the privacy era — and whether spend proves incrementality.

items: CDP/activation stacks duplicate data; costs rise with fragmentation.
Third-party identifiers deprecate; first-party identity graphs inconsistent across systems.

Governance inherits the sector frame — GDPR/ePrivacy/ATT-class among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Telecom, Media & Entertainment level this capability reads as: KubeEdge-class fleets at POPs with developer platform (edge workloads live with SLAs). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
